title: Auto Filter
text: STPHE / Auto Filter  Let recent chat choose the prompts.  An Auto Filter rule pairs a chat condition with an effect. Rules run in their numbered order.  Create a rule   Open Auto Filter and enter a name.  Choose a word, regular expression, or XML-tag condition.  Set chat depth: zero means always on; a positive number checks that many recent messages.  Choose Enable when triggered or Disable when triggered.  Select matching prompts/folders or manually chosen targets, then Add filter.   When a condition stops matching, the opposite effect applies. “Enable when triggered” disables its targets when the trigger leaves the checked chat range.  Group and order  Use ＋ Group and subgroup controls to organize rules. A muted group gates all descendant rules while preserving their individual checkboxes. Grouping does not alter execution order: numbered rule order wins when effects overlap.  Evaluation timing  Rules react to supported chat events and rule edits. Re-evaluate now runs them manually. The master Disable all filters switch pauses automatic effects without deleting rules.    Option  Meaning    Generation finishes or is aborted  Rechecks after completion, failure, or stop. Enabled by default.    Before sending (wait for filters)  Includes the new user message and awaits filter effects before request assembly. Works with Send and Enter; disabled by default.    Example: a location trigger  Create a rule matching the word  tavern  in the last four messages. Set its effect to enable a manually selected atmosphere prompt. The prompt becomes active while that word is in range and turns off when it no longer matches. Keep an unrelated base instruction outside this rule’s targets.  Check your rule  Use a small selection first. Test a matching message and a non-matching message, inspect native prompt states, and check overlapping rules. Local OpenAI-compatible mock tests covered streaming, non-streaming, abort/error recovery, group gating, and pre-send timing; real providers can differ.

title: Import, export & removal
text: STPHE / Import, export & removal  Keep a recoverable copy.  Use the Import / Export toolbar menu to transfer a hierarchy or make a backup before reorganizing it.  Export  A full export includes folder assignments, order, intended states, exclusions, saved filter presets, Auto Filter rules, and their groups. Native prompt definitions and active order are bundled when available. Folder and prompt context menus offer smaller exports.  Replace or append   Replace  replaces folder organization.  Append  adds missing organization while retaining existing local choices. Import append after an entry places imported content alongside the selected entry. Read each confirmation, especially when restoring prompt definitions.  Name conflicts  If imported and existing prompts share a name but differ in content, the conflict dialog offers choices such as keep previous, keep both, or replace. Inspect the scope before choosing a replacement.  Removal choices    Action  Result    Delete folder only  Keeps prompts and moves them up.    Remove from list  Keeps native definitions, which can be inserted again.    Delete permanently  Removes definitions and their native order references. Export first if recovery matters.    Older backups  The internal  prompt_folders  settings key and  prompt-folders  export marker remain unchanged so renaming the extension does not strand your data.

title: Folders & prompts
text: STPHE / Folders & prompts  Organize without losing intent.  Folders group prompts visually while keeping SillyTavern’s native prompt list in sync.  Mute versus force all     Control  Behavior      Folder toggle  Mutes the folder and descendants. Restoring it preserves each prompt’s intended on/off state.    Enable all  Sets every prompt in the folder and descendants on; clears overlapping folder mute state.    Disable all  Sets every prompt in the folder and descendants off; clears overlapping folder mute state.    Prompt toggle  Changes that prompt’s intended state. A muted ancestor still prevents it from being active.     Read the toggle colors    On:  intended enabled state.   Off:  disabled prompt or muted folder.   Gray suppression:  intended on, but a containing folder is muted.   Yellow mixed state:  a folder contains both intended on and intended off prompts.   The enabled count describes intended states. A separate “currently active” count appears when folder mutes suppress some of them.  Example: restoring a mixed folder  Suppose a folder contains three prompts: two enabled and one disabled. Muting the folder makes all three inactive in SillyTavern, but keeps the remembered two-on/one-off selection. Restoring the folder activates the original two prompts. Use Enable all only when you want to change the disabled prompt as well.  Nested folders  A child folder can be muted independently. Turning its parent off and back on does not erase that child mute. Unfiled is a separate bucket, not a master switch for all named folders.  Edit and preview  Use the eye control for a read-only preview and the edit control for SillyTavern’s native editor. Save in the native editor to update the prompt. Full Preview combines enabled prompt content for inspection; it is not a guarantee of the complete provider-specific request.  Move and reorder  Use move selectors or drag and drop. Ctrl/Cmd-click selects multiple entries. Moving a selected parent includes its descendants. The native prompt order follows the tree’s top-to-bottom order.  When loading ends  STPHE serializes native changes, verifies requested states, updates the tree, and waits for its paint before releasing the loading overlay. There is no fixed completion delay. Large native context calculations can still take time.

title: Getting started
text: STPHE / Getting started  Start with a small hierarchy.  STPHE runs inside SillyTavern. Use a Chat Completion API to access the native Prompt Manager it organizes.  Install   In SillyTavern, open Extensions → Install extension and use  https://github.com/miputra/STPHE . You can also obtain the files from  the STPHE repository  for a manual installation.  For manual installation, place the extension directory in your SillyTavern user’s extensions directory. Keep  manifest.json ,  index.js ,  style.css , and  src/  together.  Reload SillyTavern and enable the extension if it is disabled.  Choose Chat Completion and open AI Response Configuration once. The STPHE panel reads the native prompt list.   Upgrading from Prompt Folders? Update the existing installation. Do not install a second copy alongside it. The internal settings key and existing folder path may retain the old name intentionally.  Create your first folder   Click  Folder  in the floating panel and enter a name.  Use a prompt’s move selector to assign it to that folder.  Open the folder’s More actions menu to add a subfolder.  Toggle the folder off, then on. Its prompts keep their individual intended states.   Arrange the panel  Drag the header to move the panel. Use grow/shrink controls, resize handles, the side-switch control, and minimize/restore to fit your layout. Search filters prompts by name or identifier.  Compatibility  The current integration was checked with SillyTavern 1.18.0. Native Prompt Manager methods can change between versions. If the list is unavailable, open AI Response Configuration and press Refresh. A live API connection is needed for generation, but not for basic folder organization.

title: Overview
text: STPHE / Overview  What is STPHE?  Silly-Tavern-Prompt-Hierarchy-Expanded —  STPHE  — brings folders, reusable filter presets, and automatic prompt control to SillyTavern’s Chat Completion Prompt Manager.   Get started →  Explore folders     01 / Organize  Build a prompt hierarchy  Keep large prompt collections in folders and nested subfolders.    02 / Reuse  Group your filter presets  Save matching rules and organize them into their own hierarchy.    03 / Automate  Respond to the conversation  Enable or disable prompts when recent chat meets a condition.    What STPHE controls  The floating panel organizes the prompts in the current Chat Completion preset. Changes apply to SillyTavern’s native prompt states and order. It does not provide an AI model or API service.  Inside the extension      Real-app stress test: 500 generated prompts in 61 nested folders, alongside 12 original prompts. Screenshots were captured before the STPHE rename and show the former Prompt Folders title.   About the project  Created by  miputra . Formerly named Prompt Folders. Existing settings and exports remain compatible.  Made with Claude 4.6 Sonnet, ChatGPT 5.6 Sol, and ChatGPT 6 ASTRA.

title: Filter presets
text: STPHE / Filter presets  Save a match. Give it a home.  Filter Presets are reusable manual actions. Their groups organize the saved presets themselves, independently of prompt folders.  When should I use a preset?  Use a saved preset when you often repeat the same matching action, such as disabling prompts containing a particular XML tag. The preset stores the search and target, not a frozen list of matches. If you edit prompt content later, the next run uses that new content.  Use a prompt folder to organize the prompts themselves. Use a preset group to organize the saved actions. Use Auto Filter when an action should respond to the conversation without a manual click.  Save a filter preset   Open  Filter  from the toolbar.  Select Prompt content and choose XML tag, Word, Regex, or Regex list matching.  Enter a match and choose whether it affects prompts, their last containing folder, or all containing folders.  Enter a preset name and click Save. Applying the match first is optional.   Group saved presets   Scroll to  Filter presets  and click  ＋ Preset group .  Enter a name and save the group.  Use the group’s ＋ control to create a subgroup.  Move a preset with its group selector or drag it to a group.       A saved Filter Preset inside a nested group. Captured in the running application before the rename.   Run, lock, or mute  Enable and Disable re-evaluate the saved match against current content before applying it. Locking a preset blocks its actions. Turning a group off blocks every preset below it without changing their individual locks. Turning the group back on restores access to unlocked presets.  Groups can collapse, move, rename, and nest. Deleting a group keeps its presets and moves them up. Grouping does not execute a preset automatically.  Chat filter presets  Choose Chat in Match against to save a recent-chat condition plus a prompt/folder selection. Chat filter presets have their own groups. Their manual Enable/Disable controls check the condition and selection again when used. For automatic execution, use Auto Filter.  Exclusions  The filter exclusion control on a prompt or folder removes it from manual content matching and saved filter presets. Auto Filter has a separate exclusion control.

title: GitHub Pages
text: STPHE / GitHub Pages  Publish these docs from the repository.  The documentation is a static site. It needs no package install or external theme service.  Repository setup   Push the extension repository, including  docs/  and  .github/workflows/pages.yml , to GitHub.  Open Settings → Pages and select  GitHub Actions  as the source.  Push documentation changes to  main  or  master , or manually run the Deploy documentation workflow.  Use the Pages URL shown by the successful deployment.   The workflow uploads only  docs/ . Project-site paths work because navigation and asset URLs are relative.  Maintain the docs  Edit the HTML pages in  docs/  and shared assets in  docs/assets/ . Update  search-index.json  when changing article content. Keep screenshots free of private prompts, credentials, and account details.  Preview locally   python -m http.server 8765 --bind 127.0.0.1 --directory docs   Visit  http://127.0.0.1:8765/ . Stop the preview when finished.  Hosting reference   GitHub’s custom Pages workflow documentation  explains environment permissions and publication settings.

title: Troubleshooting
text: STPHE / Troubleshooting  Find the state that disagrees.  The panel or prompt list is missing  Confirm the extension is enabled, select Chat Completion, open AI Response Configuration, and press Refresh. Reload after updating extension files. Keep only one installation of STPHE / Prompt Folders.  Large folders feel slow  Loading should remain active until native verification and the tree paint finish. STPHE patches value changes in existing rows rather than rebuilding every selector. Context calculation and the native Prompt Manager can still be expensive. The 500-prompt test took roughly 2.7 seconds per toggle including browser-tool overhead; this is not a speed guarantee.  A saved name looks stale  Save in the native editor, then check both lists. Current STPHE reads the updated native model and observes native text/list changes. If an older copy remains loaded, reload the page. Record your SillyTavern version and whether the native name or only the STPHE name is stale.  Where are preset groups?  Open Filter, scroll to Filter presets, then choose ＋ Preset group. Chat filter presets appear when Match against is Chat. Auto Filter has its own independent group list.  An Auto Filter does not run   Check the master switch, rule checkbox, ancestor groups, and independent Auto Filter exclusions.  Check chat depth and whether the trigger is still within that range.  Use Re-evaluate now and inspect later rules that may reverse the effect.  Check invalid regular expressions and whether the selected targets still exist.   Report a reproducible problem  Include extension and SillyTavern versions, prompt/folder counts, nesting depth, reproduction steps, expected state, actual state, and a screenshot. A small sanitized export helps reproduce structural problems without sharing private prompts.
